name: casualty-string-pulse
style: British TV hospital-drama underscore, tense cinematic cue under spoken shouted dialogue, no singing; three distinct talkers: hoarse low-pitched woman in her forties, thin fast young man, booming bass older man; driving spiccato cellos and double basses racing at 150 bpm, heartbeat kick drum, wailing emergency siren, heavy rain; strings cut out hard to a ticking clock and rain; muffled plummy elderly man behind car glass; flat sine monitor beep, then dead silence; dry voice-forward mix
exclude: sung vocals, melody, chorus, choir, pop, comedy, cheerful, major key, piano, autotune, rap, reverb tail
lyrics:
[Intro: siren wail, rain, low strings racing on a heartbeat]

[Woman, hoarse, shouting]
Sixty over thirty! Fucking hurry up, we're gonna lose him!

[Young man, fast, clipped]
Sats dropping, he's peri-arrest!

[Older man, bellowing bass]
Two minutes out! Get the fuck out of the way!

[Strings stop dead. Ticking clock and rain only]

[Young man, panicked]
Why have we stopped?!

[Posh old man, muffled behind car glass]
I said raspberry-shaped hors d'oeuvres!

[Woman, quiet]
Fifty over twen—

[One long flat monitor tone, nothing under it]

[Silence]

[End]
